items.review_rationale: Reviewed connected space by impossibility of two disjoint nonempty open sets whose union covers X, with no nonempty-ambient-space requirement.

references.phrase: open subsets U and V of X
references.context: Sets declared open by the topology of X.
Both candidate open sets contain points.
No point of X belongs to both candidate open sets.
Every point of X lies in U or V.

references.disposition: Empty X admits no pair of nonempty opens and is therefore connected under this formulation.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed connectedness via trivial clopen subsets only, checking that open and closed are relative to same topological space and empty space is retained.

references.context: Subset both open in X and closed in X, equivalently C and X minus C open.
Every such C must equal empty set or all of X.

references.disposition: Equivalent clopen characterization of same connectedness meaning and convention.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed connectedness as absence of continuous surjection onto nonempty discrete two-point space, using genuine topological continuity and surjectivity on exactly two elements.

references.context: Set of exactly two distinct elements, all of whose subsets are open.

references.phrase: surjective mapping from X onto two points
references.context: Function attaining both target elements at some inputs in X.
There does not exist a mapping satisfying both continuity and surjectivity onto specified target.

references.disposition: Empty X has no surjection onto nonempty two-element target, hence satisfies this connectedness criterion.
